First Steps

KITCHEN NOTES / PREPARE BETTER

Read it twice before you touch a pan

The most common beginner mistake happens before the stove is even on. Read the whole recipe once for the plan, then once for the order.

Read → Picture → Then start
Go to the technique ↓

THE SMALL DETAILS THAT HELP

Here's how.

  1. 01

    Read the whole thing once

    Go top to bottom before touching anything — ingredients, then every step, including the ones near the end.

    Look for You should be able to say out loud what the finished dish looks like.

  2. 02

    Picture the order

    Notice which steps happen at the same time. Some things wait on the counter while others are on the stove.

    Look for If two steps say "at the same time," you have a plan for both hands.

  3. 03

    Get everything out first

    Pull every ingredient and tool onto the counter before turning on any heat.

    Look for The counter has what the recipe needs and nothing you have to search for mid-step.

  4. 04

    Start when you are not surprised

    Begin cooking once nothing on the page can catch you off guard.

    Look for The next step is never a surprise — you already read it.

A note worth keeping

Know what to look for.

You can describe the last step before you have done the first one.

Try it in a recipe ↓

AVOID THIS

Starting to cook after only skimming the ingredient list.

A recipe read halfway through hides its timing — you find out too late that something needed to happen earlier.

TRY THIS INSTEAD

Read every step before the pan goes on the heat.

MAKE SUBSTITUTIONS

Keep the job. Expect a change.

This habit works on every recipe, not just the ones on this site — only how much there is to read changes.

Still feels like too much to remember?

Keep the page open and glance at it between steps. Reading it once is about knowing the shape of the recipe, not memorizing it.
